paper.title: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures

result.summary: MatterSim 是一个基于大规模第一性原理计算、通过主动学习训练得到的深度学习原子模型，可在 0–5000 K 和 0–1000 GPa 范围内对周期表中元素组合的材料进行高效原子模拟 [abstract][S1.p3]。它作为零样本机器学习力场，在能量、力、应力预测上相比此前最优模型精度提升可达十倍 [S2.SS1.p2][S2.SS2.p1]。模型还能以接近第一性原理的精度计算晶格动力学、力学与热力学性质，例如在 1000 K 以下对无机固体的 Gibbs 自由能预测达到 15 meV/atom 的实验分辨率 [abstract][S2.SS2.p5]。此外，MatterSim 可作为持续学习与定制平台，通过微调以最多减少 97% 的数据需求完成特定任务 [abstract][S2.SS4.p2]。

research_question.text: 论文要解决的问题是：材料性质不仅取决于化学组成和近平衡原子结构，还取决于温度和压力等热力学条件，而现有数据库和模型通常只覆盖基态或局部极小结构，导致在巨大构型空间上的预测精度不足，限制了材料设计的实际应用 [S1.p2]。因此需要一种能在真实热力学条件下准确、高效预测任意材料性质的方法 [S1.p1][S1.p3]。

evidence.quote: At the core of this paradigm shift is the ability to accurately and efficiently predict the properties of arbitrary materials under practical synthesis and working conditions.

However, the property of a potential candidate material not only depends on its chemical composition and corresponding near-equilibrium atomic structure, but also on thermodynamic conditions including temperature and pressure.

This results in a requirement of high predictive accuracy over an enormous configuration space well beyond the ground states or local minima of crystal structures typically captured by current databases and models, which fundamentally limits their applicability for materials design.

To address this challenge, we introduce MatterSim, a deep learning model designed for emulating materials and predicting their properties under realistic thermodynamic conditions including finite temperatures and pressures

method.text: MatterSim 采用主动学习框架，整合深度图神经网络、材料探索器、第一性原理监督器和集成不确定性监测器 [S2.SS1.p1]。第一性原理监督器在 GGA-PBE 水平（对部分材料加 Hubbard U 修正）提供能量、力和应力标签，模型作为代理引导探索器采样高不确定性区域，形成主动学习循环 [S2.SS1.p1]。模型骨干采用 M3GNet 和 Graphormer 两种架构，其中 Graphormer 为基于 transformer 的模型并加入了平移不变性、周期性边界条件和显式等变特征 [S2.SS1.p3]。

evidence.quote: MatterSim employs an active learning approach to explore the extensive materials space, integrating a deep graph neural network, a materials explorer, a first-principles supervisor, and an ensemble uncertainty monitor

the first-principles supervisor offers the deep learning model supervision signals relating to energies, forces, and stresses on the given structures at the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE) level of theory with Hubbard U correction for select materials

This trained model then functions as an effective surrogate to the first-principles method, guiding the materials explorer to gather more structures, thereby exploring the most uncertain regions of materials space to enrich the samples for model training.
In this work, we opt to use two primary architectures, M3GNet and Graphormer as the backbones for MatterSim.

Graphormer is a transformer-based model with proven learning capacity and scalability. In particular, we baked in several additional attributes including invariance to translation and periodic boundary conditions and explicit equivariant features to better accommodate materials-related tasks

experiments.text: 训练数据集包含约 1700 万个第一性原理标注结构，覆盖 0–5000 K 和 0–1000 GPa 的温度压力范围 [S2.SS1.p2]。零样本性能在多个基准上评估，包括 MPtrj-1k、Alexandria-1k、MPtrj-highest-stress-1k，以及新创建的 MPF-Alkali-TP、MPF-TP 和 Random-TP 数据集，后者由第一性原理分子动力学轨迹采样，温度 0–5000 K、压力 0–1000 GPa [S6.p1][S6.p2]。此外还在 PhononDB 声子数据库、MatBench Discovery、MatBench 回归任务以及 118 个系统的分子动力学模拟上进行了验证 [S2.SS2.p3][S2.SS2.p2][S2.SS5.p2][S2.SS2.p6]。

evidence.quote: As of the date of publication, the training dataset contains $\sim$ 17M structures labeled with first-principles computations.
As shown in Fig. 2 (b), the curated dataset is representative of materials at temperatures and pressures covering 0– $5000\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ and 0– $1000\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa}$.
MPtrj-1k and Alexandria-1k are collected by sampling randomly one thousand materials from the MPtrj and Alexandria dataset, respectively.

The MPF-Alkali-TP, MPF-TP, Random-TP benchmark sets are created with increasing complexity to evaluate the models’ performance on materials under finite temperature and pressure conditions with far from equilibrium atomic positions.
For the temperature, it is uniformly sampled between 0 to 5000K. For the pressure, we used a log scale when carrying out the sampling. The pressure range is from 0 to 1000 GPa.
Fig. 4 (a) shows the benchmark results on the materials from the PhononDB, using maximum phonon frequency as an indicator

MatterSim shows a strong capability in predicting stability of new materials, with an F1 score of 0.83 and a mean absolute energy error of the formation energy of $25\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ benchmarked on MatBench Discovery

MatterSim’s capability to directly predict materials properties from structures is benchmarked on a few regression tasks from MatBench, including prediction of computed band gaps, shear moduli, dielectric constants, max phonon frequency of bulk crystalline materials, and the exfoliation energies of two-dimensional materials.
we randomly selected 118 systems including bulk inorganic materials, metal organic frameworks, two-dimensional materials, interfaces, molecular crystals, polymers and surfaces

findings.text: MatterSim 在 MPF-TP 和 Random-TP 等高温高压数据集上相比此前最优通用力场精度提升可达十倍 [S2.SS1.p2][S2.SS2.p1]。在 MatBench Discovery 上取得 F1 分数 0.83 和 25 meV/atom 的形成能平均绝对误差 [S2.SS2.p2]。声子最大频率预测 MAE 为 0.87 THz，0 K 体模量 MAE 为 2.47 GPa [S2.SS2.p3][S2.SS2.p4]。自由能预测在 1000 K 以下与 PBE 计算误差低于 10 meV/atom，与 200 多个材料的实验测量相比 MAE 为 15 meV/atom [S2.SS2.p5]。在 118 个系统的分子动力学模拟中，所有材料类别的成功率超过 90% [S2.SS2.p6]。

evidence.quote: The most noticeable enhancement are observed on the benchmark datasets MPF-TP and Random-TP (sampled from high temperature and pressure), where MatterSim achieves up to 10-fold improvement compared to universal force fields trained on relaxation trajectories.
MatterSim outperforms force fields trained on open relaxation trajectory databases with a substantial increase in accuracy by an order of magnitude compared to previous best-in-class

MatterSim shows a strong capability in predicting stability of new materials, with an F1 score of 0.83 and a mean absolute energy error of the formation energy of $25\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ benchmarked on MatBench Discovery
a good agreement is achieved with a mean absolute error (MAE) of $0.87\text{\,}\mathrm{THz}$.
A remarkable agreement is achieved with an MAE of only $2.47\text{\,}\mathrm{GPa}$.

MatterSim achieves a sub- $10\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$ error for temperatures up to $1000\text{\,}\mathrm{K}$ when compared with QHA computations at PBE level of theory

when compared with experimental measurements on over 200 materials as shown in Fig. S22, it achieves an MAE of $15\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{e}\mathrm{V}\mathrm{/}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{m}$
As shown in Fig. 5 (b), MatterSim achieved more than 90% success rate for all the material families tested, exhibiting robustness over wide temperature ranges.

limitations.text: 作者指出，MatterSim 目前采用半局域原子相互作用描述，在长程相互作用主导性质的情形（如聚合物和异质系统）中表现不佳 [S3.p3]。模型仅在均匀体相系统上训练，未显式包含对催化等应用至关重要的表面和界面数据 [S3.p3]。模型目前仅原生支持 DFT-PBE 水平的推断，限制了其在涉及复杂相互作用的系统（如聚合物和有机液体）中的使用 [S3.p3]。此外，模型目前仅支持能量、力和应力的原生预测，纳入电荷、自旋、磁矩等更多数据模态可能进一步提升精度和适用性 [S3.p3]。

evidence.quote: it currently utilizes a semi-local description of atomic interactions, where long-range interactions majorly leverages message passing or updates on attention weights through graph nodes.
it doesn’t perform effectively in scenarios where long-range interactions dominate the properties, such as polymeric and heterogeneous systems.
the current model is trained only on homogeneous bulk systems, without explicit inclusion of surface and interface data that are crucial for applications such as catalysis.
the model currently only naively supports inferences with DFT-PBE level of theory, limiting its use for systems involving complex interactions, such as polymers and organic liquids.

Currently, the model only supports the native prediction of energy, forces, and stresses. Including more data modalities, such as charge, spin, magnetic moments, and even more complex electronic structure features, could further enhance the model’s accuracy and applicability.
